questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Japan was a country that for a long time had my interest in both an academically and personally.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I abseloutly loved my time there!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was somewhat difficult, but not unmanageable.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received a lot of information by mail from my host university, which for the most parts was sufficent.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was recommended some dormitories by my host university, which I applied for.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I technecliy lived off campus, but I only had a 6 minute walk to campus, so I couldn't really tell,

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I lived at a dormitory connected to my university, which was nice and nearby, and I lived with multiple classmates, which I loved!

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Not that complicated, but you do not register until about two weeks before classes began, which was a bit stressful.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Not that much, there was a website, but it was not super intuitive, but has dorm-mates helping me out.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I think I got 7 out of the 8 courses I wanted the most, but I really enjoyed my eighth course that I haven't planned for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not to stress to much about late course registration, it's just how it works there.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was my first time taking classes in english, so I choose to take some "easier" courses, which was a manageable level.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Somewhat different, but each class were quite different, some being more or less like the teaching of UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I thought that especially: "Aging and the Life Course", "Game Theory", "Labour Market in the Global Economy" amd "Examining Global Issues 1" was really interesting, and I would recommend these courses to future exchange students.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Most items were less expensive than I expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Many options, but you have to be quick when you arrive if you want to join a club, I started bouldering with some friends outside of the clubs at the school.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I ended up during stuff on my own with friends, so I do not have much to recommend, but bouldering is a lot of fun!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: See Kyoto, Osaka, Nara, Hiroshima, and maybe even travel outside of the country (quite easy, but you have to do a bit of paperwork in the airport).

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite overwhelming the first two weeks, so I recommend traveling to the exchange site a couple of weeks before the classes start.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Not really, just remember that other exchange student are also far from home and looking for friends and to socialize!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Hmm honeslty japanese people are a lot like danes, just more polite.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: the politeness and kindness!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
If you go to Waseda:
1. You should apply for WID WASEDA dorm, its cozy and very close by!
2. There is a beautiful garden where you can relax and enjoy your lunch, use it!
3. Even though Waseda is the largest international university in Japan, a lot of locals still don't speak english that well, so you will get far by learning a few phrases in Japanese.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Its a pretty big campus, so make sure to get a picture of the campus ground for the first couple of weeks.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friends I made there.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Much uncertainty about how things worked and if they would work out. Also I received no grants cause I applied too late, which was a big blow.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
